title: The Day Of Divine Punishment
paragraphs: “Then I’d like you to come with me. Once we save Éclair, we have no more business here.”
Well, technically, there’s still more to do…
“Got it.”
“Not like we really have the right to refuse.”
“Without Motoyasu-san, we probably wouldn’t even be able to make it out of here alive.”

From earlier, all I’ve been hearing is shouts of “Kill them! Kill them!” After I prevented Father from being falsely accused, they decided to pin the title of “False Hero” on me instead. That scumbag and the crimson swine sure left behind a nasty little parting gift. Oh well. The people in this castle don’t seem to understand what happens when you defy a Hero. The exit from the throne room isn’t too far, but the soldiers have gathered throughout the castle. Stepping into the hallway, I see them struggling against my wall of fire. Looks like a few of them have already been turned to charcoal.
“I-it’s the False Hero! Kill him immediately!”
“Has anyone checked on the king!?”
“That man no longer exists in this world. Paralyze Lance!”
While shifting the wall of fire, I struck them with my lance, paralyzing them. Looks like they’ve finally realized my strength—some of the soldiers have started clearing a path.
“If even one of you so much as lifts a finger, I’ll slaughter you all.”
I glared at them, and they froze in fear.
“Now then, let’s be on our way.”

Father and the others held their breath as they followed me. But then, suddenly, a shadowy figure appeared and threw poisoned needles at us. I deflected them with my lance and drove it straight through him.
“Enough of this nonsense.”
“How many of them are there…?”
“They’re determined not to let us escape.”
Eventually, we made it to the castle entrance. By now, not just the soldiers, but also members of the Three Heroes Church had shown up. They must’ve used the commotion as an excuse to gather.
“Let’s show them just how foolish it is to stand against a Hero.”
“W-what are you planning to do?”
Ren was the one to ask.
“Do you see that building over there?”
I pointed toward a large church near the plaza beyond the castle gate. The Three Heroes Church.
“Yeah, what about it?”
“The masterminds behind this entire conspiracy—the real culprits—should be there.”
The Pope is definitely inside. After all, today was supposed to be the day when Father was falsely accused. I bet he was watching in amusement as Father walked around in nothing but his underclothes.
“You’re not seriously thinking of barging in there, are you?”
Father stepped in and asked. That’s not my plan, but…
“If you wish, I can take out the mastermind right before your eyes. What do you say?”
“That’s not what I meant! You are planning to storm in, aren’t you!?”
“No, I wouldn’t bother with something so tedious.”
“R-right… That’s a relief.”
“There’s no need to even step inside the building.”
“…What?”
I focus my consciousness and begin chanting my spell.
“Liberation Firestorm X!”

I conjure a sphere that generates a raging storm of fire and hurl it with precision. With a sharp whoosh, it arcs through the air in a grand trajectory. The moment it bursts above the church, a powerful tornado of flames erupts. A blazing inferno that pierces the heavens themselves. Father and the others stare in stunned silence as the swirling flames and wind rage before them.
“Rest assured. The spell is targeted only at the church—civilians remain unharmed.”
“Th-th-th-th-that’s not the issue here!?”
“So this… this is the strength of a Hero?”
“Is this how strong we’ll become too!?”
“Of course! Ren, Itsuki, this level of power should be nothing for you both!”
Hearing my praise, Ren and Itsuki continue gazing at the inferno.
“I can’t say I’m happy to have your endorsement…”
“Agreed. I just want to go home already…”
“What about me?”

“Father, your role is support and healing. You can’t learn direct offensive magic. However, you will master spells that enhance our strength even beyond this. You’ll grant us power far greater than this.”
“…I should probably hold off on asking why you know that, huh? Given that we’re still being pursued.”
With the Three Heroes Church now reduced to ashes, the soldiers have also lost their will to fight. Many of them collapse onto the ground in despair.
“Ahh… The gods have delivered judgment upon us fools…”
“A church that could withstand ritual magic was destroyed so effortlessly…!”
“This is the day of divine punishment…”
Some have begun clasping their hands in prayer. Those with deep faith merely pray and beg for their lives instead of resisting.
“This should make things easier for us.”
“After pulling off something like that, yeah, I’d imagine so…”
Father replies, sounding weary. I’d like some praise, though.
“Now we just need to evade any lingering assassins and head to the underground prison.”
“A prison…? So they’re a criminal?”
“If I recall correctly, their charge was executing soldiers from a nation that engaged in slave hunting.”
“Slaves…”
“That doesn’t sound like a crime. If anything, that seems like the right thing to do…”
Itsuki tilts his head in confusion.

“In the demi-human sanctuary where Father is revered, a noble was killed during a Wave. After that, slave hunting began, and this person fought to protect the victims. Though, in this country, that’s considered a crime.”
Itsuki’s sense of justice must have been stirred, as his determination seems to be returning.
“Yeah, considering they’re the kind of people who’d try to kill us just because they don’t like the outcome, this person sounds decent from what we’ve heard.”
“I’m not sure if we’ll get along, though. They seemed rather serious.”
Éclair did seem serious, even to me.
I believe we can communicate if we talk, but who knows?
“Alright, let’s go.”

We headed straight to the underground prison. The castle town was growing more chaotic by the minute. Father, clad in chainmail, looked uneasy. I’d like to get him somewhere safe and calm as soon as possible. We moved through the prison, illuminating our path with fire magic. Father and the others looked around, concerned about the people locked in their cells. It was a stone-built, damp, and utterly miserable place.
“…So they really do have prisons here.”
“In a country like this, they probably throw in anyone they don’t like.”
“Huh? That person… their ears… Are they a demi-human? Well, I guess that makes sense in another world.”
“I saw some in the castle town yesterday.”
“Yeah. They were probably captured just for being demi-humans.”
Just like last time, the prisoners had no energy left in them. They likely hadn’t even noticed that we were otherworlders, assuming us to be just more soldiers.
“We shouldn’t go around freeing people carelessly, should we?”
“Yeah… There could be some truly dangerous criminals mixed in here. It’s probably best if we don’t get too involved.”
“Exactly. We need to figure out what the right course of action is first.”

Eventually, we arrived at the cell where I had previously met Éclair. I peered inside through the iron bars. She was still alive. Father and the others gasped at the sight of her. She was suspended by shackles, forced to stand, and bore clear signs of torture.
“Hey, I don’t recognize you. Are you a soldier of Melromarc? There’s been a lot of commotion—did something happen?”
“What are you staring at? Do you enjoy looking at me that much?”
“There’s nothing enjoyable about this…”
Father was the first to respond.
“So this country does things like this without a second thought, huh…”
“Motoyasu, is this the person?”
“That’s right.”
“It’s dark, so I can’t see well, but… she looks pretty, doesn’t she?”
Éclair looked at us, exhausted, utterly exasperated. She probably thought we were just some lost rookie soldiers.
“Um, are you Éclair?”
Father asked on behalf of the group.
“Who are you talking about? You’ve got the wrong person.”
